method: Read-only static analysis via 7 parallel domain subagents; no fixes applied; no production probing.

stack_actual.api: Fastify + Prisma + PostgreSQL (no Postgres RLS; tenant isolation enforced in application code)
stack_actual.auth: Custom JWT via @fastify/jwt (HS256), Bearer tokens in localStorage, no cookies
stack_actual.frontends: Vite + React SPAs (apps/web, apps/admin, apps/driver) on Vercel/Cloudflare Pages
stack_actual.storage: Supabase Storage bucket pod-photos (public-read per docs/DEPLOYMENT.md)

findings.title: Vulnerable fast-jwt in production JWT authentication path
findings.evidence: pnpm audit --prod returns 6 advisories, all fast-jwt (3 critical/1 high/2 moderate): empty-HMAC-secret JWT bypass (fix >=6.2.4), RS256->HS256 algorithm confusion (incomplete CVE-2023-48223 fix, >=6.2.0), cacheKeyBuilder cache confusion, crit-header bypass CVE-2026-35042, 2x ReDoS. @fastify/jwt ^9 pulls the vulnerable line.
findings.remediation: Bump @fastify/jwt to ^10.1.0 (patched fast-jwt >=6.2.4); validate v9->v10 against registerAuth; assert non-empty JWT_SECRET at boot in config.ts; re-run pnpm audit --prod.

findings.title: SSRF via tenant-controlled outbound URLs (3 sinks, one a response oracle)
findings.evidence: z.string().url() accepts any scheme/host. /clients/test-webhook fetches an arbitrary URL and returns {ok,status} (internal-network/metadata oracle). Developer webhooks and per-client webhookUrl are stored SSRF delivered on events and via /test endpoints; lastStatus persisted. No private-CIDR/metadata block, no scheme allowlist, no DNS-rebind protection.
findings.remediation: Centralized safeFetch(): restrict scheme to http(s), resolve host and reject loopback/private/link-local/CGNAT/metadata ranges and *.internal, redirect:'error', pin resolved IP. Validate at write-time (Zod refine) and delivery-time.

findings.title: POD delivery evidence (PII) served from public Supabase bucket / unauthenticated /files/
findings.evidence: storage.ts returns .../object/public/${bucket}/${key}; bucket pod-photos documented public-read. Dev /files/ static route has no auth and no Cache-Control. Keys are 96-bit random (not enumerable) but protection rests entirely on URL secrecy; public objects are freely CDN-cacheable with no revocation; cross-tenant on leak. POD = PII / B2B dispute evidence.
findings.remediation: Make pod-photos private; serve via short-TTL signed URLs (Cache-Control: private) or an authenticated tenant-scoped streaming endpoint (verify route.tenantId === req.user.tenantId). Add auth + no-store to dev /files/ or do not register it when internet-exposed.
findings.owasp_2025: A01 Broken Access Control / A02 Security Misconfiguration

findings.title: Global rate limiter is per-instance in-memory and not proxy-aware (no trustProxy)
findings.evidence: Fastify constructor sets no trustProxy; @fastify/rate-limit {global:true,max:300,timeWindow:'1 minute'} with no Redis store and no keyGenerator (default key request.ip). Counters reset/multiply across Render instances; request.ip is the edge socket IP behind the proxy, collapsing clients or hiding the real client. Per-route caps inherit the weakness.
findings.remediation: Set trustProxy:true (or hop count); back rate-limit with a shared Redis store; add a keyGenerator factoring tenant/API-key on authenticated routes.

findings.title: Ingest order-creation endpoints have no per-route rate limit
findings.evidence: POST /ingest/orders and /ingest/orders/:source carry only requireApiScope('orders:write') with no config.rateLimit; they call createOrder (DB writes + geocoding cascade + webhook fan-out). Bounded only by the soft global 300/min (unreliable per MO-04). No per-key quota.
findings.remediation: Add a tighter per-route rateLimit keyed by API key; enforce a per-tenant/per-key daily order quota tied to the plan.

findings.title: Tenant ADMIN can self-enable paid modules (paywall/entitlement bypass)
findings.evidence: Tenant-plane PATCH /modules/:key does moduleEntitlement.upsert(...enabled:true...) blocking only CORE_MODULE_KEYS. Paid modules (TELEMATICS, SAFETY, ANALYTICS_PRO, AI_ADDONS, CUSTOMER_EXPERIENCE_PRO, COMPLIANCE_RNDC, COLD_CHAIN; core:false) can be enabled by a customer admin with no billing/platform check. A platform-admin override exists in parallel, indicating self-enable is unintended.
findings.remediation: Remove enable-side self-service from the tenant plane (allow disable/downgrade only, or enable only plan-included modules); route enable through the platform/billing plane.

findings.title: No dependency/SCA gate in CI; no Dependabot/Renovate
findings.evidence: CI runs install/generate/migrate/build/test with no pnpm audit, SCA, or secret scan. No dependabot.yml/renovate.json. Root cause that MO-01's critical chain shipped unnoticed.
findings.remediation: Add CI step pnpm audit --prod --audit-level=high (fail on prod high/critical); add .github/dependabot.yml for npm/pnpm (weekly, grouped).

findings.title: Stateless JWT cannot be revoked (logout/reset/delete do not invalidate live tokens)
findings.evidence: Tokens signed {expiresIn:'12h'} with no tokenVersion/jti. No /logout endpoint; frontend logout clears localStorage only. Code documents that reset/delete does not revoke existing JWTs (<=12h). Tenant suspension is re-checked live, but identity/role/password changes are not.
findings.remediation: Add a tokenVersion/passwordChangedAt claim compared in verifyTenantToken/requirePlatformAdmin (bump = real logout), or a short jti denylist with TTL=remaining exp.

findings.title: Self-service /auth/register: no rate limit/CAPTCHA, unverified email, auto-grants ADMIN
findings.evidence: /login is throttled 10/min but /auth/register has no rate limit and no CAPTCHA; it creates Tenant+entitlements+ADMIN user and issues a 12h ADMIN token with no email verification. Role is server-hardcoded (no privilege escalation into existing tenant), but mass-signup abuse and unverified-email account creation are open.
findings.remediation: Add a tight per-route limit (e.g. 5/min/IP) + CAPTCHA; require email verification before issuing an operational token.

findings.title: Address /validate paid-geocoder cost-amplification (only the soft global limit)
findings.evidence: POST /addresses/validate -> geocodeAddress runs the paid LUPAP/Google cascade with only the global 300/min. Novel strings bypass the Address-Graph cache, enabling authenticated financial-DoS on paid providers.
findings.remediation: Per-tenant per-route rateLimit on /addresses/validate; meter paid-provider calls against plan usage.

findings.title: SPAs have no committed hosting security headers (CSP/frame-ancestors)
findings.evidence: helmet protects only API JSON. The SPA HTML (clickjacking/CSP surface) is served by Vercel/Cloudflare Pages with no headers/_headers/CSP/frame-ancestors committed; vite configs set none.
findings.remediation: Commit explicit host headers per SPA: CSP with frame-ancestors 'self', X-Content-Type-Options nosniff, Referrer-Policy, HSTS. Verify via securityheaders.com.

findings.title: Failed logins are not logged (no security event stream)
findings.evidence: 401 on bad credentials/unknown email/suspended tenant with no app.log line and no audit record. Credential-stuffing/lockout patterns invisible to ops.
findings.remediation: app.log.warn({event:'auth.login_failed', email, ip}) (email only, never password) on each 401; optional per-account failed-attempt counter.
findings.owasp_2025: A09 Security Logging and Alerting Failures

findings.title: Webhook delivery failures swallowed by bare catch (no log/Sentry)
findings.evidence: deliverWebhook catches failures with bare catch {} recording only lastStatus:0; emitWebhookEvent discards Promise.allSettled results. No app.log/captureError. Integrations can silently stop with zero visibility.
findings.remediation: Log a warn with webhook.id/tenantId/url/status (no secret) on failure; captureError on repeated failures; surface lastStatus in the developer UI.
findings.owasp_2025: A09 Security Logging and Alerting Failures

findings.title: TOCTOU idempotency on order ingest and POD completion (not DB-enforced)
findings.evidence: createOrder dedups via findFirst({tenantId,externalRef}) then inserts with no @@unique([tenantId,externalRef]) and no transaction -> concurrent retries duplicate orders. POD completion checks status==='COMPLETED' then updates routeStop by id only (no status precondition) -> concurrent offline-queue replays both emit DELIVERED webhooks/events.
findings.remediation: Add @@unique([tenantId,externalRef]) + upsert/catch P2002 in createOrder; make POD update conditional (updateMany where status != 'COMPLETED', check count).

findings.title: Public tracking JSON returns recipient PII + live driver GPS with no cache headers
findings.evidence: GET /track/:token returns recipient, address, operator, sender, driverPosition{lat,lng,at} (FULL tier) with no Cache-Control. Token-keyed private data that must not be shared-cache eligible.
findings.remediation: Set reply.header('Cache-Control','no-store') on /track/:token and its 404 path.

findings.title: JWT stored in localStorage across all SPAs (XSS-readable)
findings.evidence: moveos_token / moveos_driver_token / moveos_platform_token in localStorage, attached as Authorization: Bearer. Any XSS exfiltrates a 12h token; the admin token grants cross-tenant platform access. (Also why CSRF is N/A.)
findings.remediation: Prefer httpOnly+Secure+SameSite cookies (then add CSRF tokens) or keep tokens short-lived + revocable (MO-08) behind a strict CSP; keep dangerouslySetInnerHTML banned.

findings.title: Driver logout leaves PII in on-device storage
findings.evidence: Logout runs only setToken(null). moveos_driver_route (names/addresses), moveos_driver_queue (queued delivery POST bodies, POD URLs), moveos_driver_chargers persist in localStorage. On a shared device the next holder reads prior PII via DevTools.
findings.remediation: On logout clear those keys and caches.delete() non-tile caches; warn if the offline queue is non-empty before discarding.
findings.owasp_2025: A02 / A05 (sensitive data in client cache)

findings.title: DISPATCHER (any staff) can read tenant billing/cost via non-ADMIN GET handlers
findings.evidence: GET /controls/cost and /controls/billing require only app.authenticate while their PATCH counterparts require ADMIN. They return driverCostPerHourCop, energyTariffCop, legalName/nit/billingEmail/billingAddress, invoices. SPA hides the nav but mounts the route for DISPATCHER. Role-scoping gap, not cross-tenant.
findings.remediation: Add requireRole('ADMIN') to these GET handlers if billing/cost is ADMIN-only.

findings.title: @fastify/multipart registered with no global limits
findings.evidence: register(multipart) with no limits; only the POD handler caps fileSize (8MB). Field/part counts and any future multipart consumer are unbounded -> resource-exhaustion via thousands of parts/huge fields.
findings.remediation: register(multipart,{limits:{fileSize:8*1024*1024,files:1,fields:10,parts:20}}), keeping per-route overrides.

findings.title: No Cache-Control: no-store on authenticated API JSON (back-button after logout)
findings.location: apps/api/src/app.ts (no default Cache-Control; only SSE sets no-cache)
findings.evidence: No authenticated JSON route sets no-store; grep for no-store across apps/ returns zero. Bounded by Bearer-token auth (no ambient cookie) but defense-in-depth wants no-store given shared-device risk (MO-17).
findings.remediation: Add an onSend hook setting Cache-Control: no-store on non-public, non-asset routes.

findings.title: Login user-enumeration via bcrypt timing side-channel
findings.evidence: bcrypt.compare is short-circuited when the email is unknown (!user), so existing emails pay the hash cost (~tens of ms) and unknown ones do not. Response body is correctly uniform ('Credenciales invalidas'); only timing leaks existence.
findings.remediation: Always compare against a fixed dummy bcrypt hash when the user is not found (constant work). Confirm the delta in deployment.

findings.title: Sentry/alerting off-by-default in production (SENTRY_DSN empty in blueprint)
findings.evidence: captureError no-ops when SENTRY_DSN is unset; render.yaml ships it empty (sync:false). On a fresh deploy all 5xx go to logs only. Positive: captureError sends only the exception, never request bodies/headers/tokens.
findings.remediation: Make SENTRY_DSN (or an equivalent alert sink) a required go-live checklist item.
findings.owasp_2025: A09 Security Logging and Alerting Failures

findings.title: Deleted/missing tenant (status null) is not blocked - only SUSPENDED is
findings.evidence: getTenantStatus returns null for a missing/deleted tenant; the gate blocks only status==='SUSPENDED', so a deleted tenant's outstanding 12h tokens still authenticate the operational plane.
findings.remediation: Treat status !== 'ACTIVE' (including null) as 403 in auth.ts.

findings.title: POD upload MIME validated by client-declared type, not magic bytes
findings.evidence: MIME comes from the multipart Content-Type, not content sniffing. Impact limited: extension forced from the allowlist, helmet nosniff, server-randomized filename (no traversal/SVG-XSS). A polyglot can still be stored as .png.
findings.remediation: Verify magic bytes (e.g. file-type) match the declared image; ensure POD served as image/attachment, never text/html.

findings.title: Prod SPA builds may ship JS source maps (no explicit sourcemap:false)
findings.evidence: Vite build.sourcemap defaults to false but is not explicitly locked; if a build flips it on, .map files expose frontend source. No secrets live in SPA bundles, so impact is attack-surface mapping.
findings.remediation: Set build:{sourcemap:false} in all three configs; confirm no *.map in dist/.

findings.title: HSTS max-age is helmet's 180-day default (no preload)
findings.evidence: register(helmet) with no opts -> Strict-Transport-Security: max-age=15552000; includeSubDomains (180 days, no preload).
findings.remediation: Optional: helmet({hsts:{maxAge:31536000,includeSubDomains:true,preload:true}}) if MoveOS controls the apex and wants preload.

findings.title: Weak hardcoded dev JWT secret fallback (prod boot guard present and correct)
findings.evidence: DEV_JWT_SECRET constant used as a dev fallback, but a prod guard throws if isProd && (secret===DEV || length<32); render.yaml auto-generates a strong JWT_SECRET. No production exposure; no rotation required.
findings.remediation: Optional hardening: derive the dev fallback from a per-machine random value so it is not a constant.

findings.title: Demo seed credentials are public/documented (moveos123)
findings.evidence: bcrypt.hash('moveos123',10) seeding *.demo.moveos.co accounts, password documented in the seed header and tests. Intentional fixtures (hashed, not plaintext); risk only if seeded against a public prod DB.
findings.remediation: Gate the seed behind NODE_ENV !== 'production' / never run against the prod DB; optionally source the demo password from an env var.

findings.title: weightKg and similar operational numerics are client-trusted on order creation
findings.evidence: CLIENT-supplied weightKg (positive-number only) feeds capacity/optimizer math. No price is computed client-side (price derives from server-validated serviceId), so this is trusted-input-affecting-planning, not price tampering. No isolation impact.
findings.remediation: Accept as designed, or bound/validate against service constraints if weight ever drives billing.

findings.title: No explicit Fastify bodyLimit (relies on 1 MB default)
findings.evidence: No bodyLimit set; Fastify default 1 MB applies (cap exists but is not intentional/auditable). Malformed/empty JSON is handled cleanly (try/catch -> 400, no crash).
findings.remediation: Set an explicit bodyLimit matching real needs; rely on @fastify/multipart limits for uploads (MO-19).

findings.title: <500 business errors echo err.message verbatim (no concrete leak found)
findings.evidence: Error handler returns err.message for statusCode<500; 5xx always returns generic 'Error interno'. Observed 4xx messages are deliberate Spanish business strings; no internal/DB/stack leak found, but a future library error with a 4xx code would pass its message through.
findings.remediation: Whitelist/known 4xx messages; ensure thrown 4xx errors never embed DB/driver text.

findings.title: Dev-tooling CVEs (vitest/vite/esbuild) - not in the production image
findings.evidence: pnpm audit flags vitest <3.2.6 (UI arbitrary file read, critical), vite server.fs.deny bypass (high), esbuild dev-server CORS (moderate/low). All require a running dev server / Vitest UI; devDependencies, not in the Render prod build. Top-level vite@6.4.3 is already patched.
findings.remediation: Bump vitest ^3.2.6; resolve vite >=6.4.3 consistently to clear the audit so the MO-07 CI gate stays green.

findings.title: .gitignore lacks *.pem/*.key/*.p12/.env.*.local patterns
findings.evidence: Covers .env and .env.local but not *.pem/*.key/*.p12/*.pfx/.env.production/.env.*.local. No such files exist today; this is preventive hardening.
findings.remediation: Add the patterns to prevent accidental future commits of key/cert/env files.

reviewed_sound_no_action: Secrets: no hardcoded provider keys (all process.env); no server secret in any VITE_ client bundle; git history clean (pickaxe scans); API keys SHA-256, webhook secrets HMAC, shown once.
Injection: all $queryRaw tagged-template parameterized; no Unsafe/Prisma.raw/string-SQL; no eval/Function/child_process; orderBy uses static field names.
XSS: zero dangerouslySetInnerHTML/innerHTML/document.write across SPAs; React default escaping; no markdown/HTML renderer.
CSRF: N/A - Bearer-header auth, no cookies (@fastify/cookie absent).

Tenant isolation/IDOR: update/delete-by-id preceded by tenant-scoped findFirst -> 404; bare findUnique({id}) are token-derived or platform-admin by design; findUnique({email}) are uniqueness checks only.
Platform plane: requirePlatformAdmin rejects tenant tokens (403); impersonation 30-min, audited, never CLIENT, tenant-scoped.
Auth provenance: tenantId/role/driverId/clientId only from verified JWT; signup hardcodes ADMIN, portal hardcodes CLIENT.
Supply chain: no hallucinated/typosquatted packages; lockfile committed.
Logging: no secrets/PII logged; platform audit redacts passwords; Sentry sends only exceptions.

Cache: driver service worker caches only /assets/, shell, OSM tiles - API/uploads bypass SW cache; no cache poisoning (no X-Forwarded-Host reflection); no Set-Cookie/token in cacheable response; web cache deception N/A.
Password reset: admin-mediated only (no self-service token to attack); aligns with B2B-only notifications.
